memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, but you have done nothing but bless them!" He answered, "Must I not speak what the LORD puts in my mouth?" - Num 23:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balak is furious. He brought Balaam to curse his enemies, and instead the prophet has blessed them. His investment has produced the opposite of what he wanted. In his anger he demands, "What have you done to me?" as if Balaam had betrayed the arrangement.

But Balaam's reply is the heart of the matter: must he not speak what the Lord puts in his mouth? He had no freedom to say otherwise. The word belonged to God, not to Balak, not even to Balaam. However much silver changed hands, the message could only be what God gave.

This confronts us with an important truth about God's word. It is not ours to shape according to our wishes or the wishes of those who would pay for a different message. God's word stands firm, and faithfulness means speaking what He has said, not what people want to hear. This can be costly, as it disappointed a king here.

We live in a world that often wants a different word from the one God has spoken. Yet like Balaam in this moment, we are called to speak the truth God has given, not the message that pleases the crowd. In Christ, we hold fast to God's word even when it is unwelcome, for His word alone endures forever (1 Pet 1:25).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you ever tempted to soften God's word to please others?
2. What does faithfulness to God's word cost you?
3. How can you hold fast to God's truth even when it is unwelcome?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me courage to speak Your word faithfully, even when others want a different message. Keep me from softening Your truth to please the crowd. Amen.
